title: Field certification, tenant burn-in, and operator runbook for private deployments
author: Evelyn Chong
content:
Overview

Purpose
This document defines the field certification and tenant burn-in program for Redwood Private deployments (VPC and on-prem), plus an operator runbook to guide installation teams through post-install validation, acceptance, and safe handoff to steady-state operations. It is intended for field engineers, SREs, integration engineers, and customer success teams.

Scope
- Applies to all private deployments delivered with Redwood-managed control plane or customer-managed control plane.
- Covers hardware and firmware verification, runtime sanity tests, tenant-specific workload burn-in, telemetry contract validation, licensing and KMS key rotation, and defined acceptance criteria for Customer Acceptance Testing (CAT).

Assumptions and prerequisites
- Operator has network access to customer telemetry endpoints as specified in the integration contract.
- Images and packages are signed (see container-image-signing-and-verification-playbook).
- Required keys and certificates are provisioned in the target KMS/HSM and accessible to the installation environment.

Approval and ownership
- Program owner: eng-private-deployments Field Engineering (owner: Marco Ruiz)
- Certification authority: Security & Compliance (reviewer: Dr. Lena Fischer)
- Final acceptance signer: Customer Success lead for the customer account

High-level workflow (summary)
1. Pre-flight verification (lab)
2. Field install and bootstrap
3. Hardware & firmware attestation
4. Runtime smoke and KV/Prefix cache warmup
5. Tenant-specific synthetic burn-in (hours or days depending on SLAs)
6. Telemetry validation and evidence collection
7. CAT sign-off and handoff to operations

Detailed procedures

1) Pre-flight verification (lab stage)
- Duration: 2–8 hours per image revision.
- Steps:
  a. Verify signed images match shipped digest: sha256 checksums for every artifact.
  b. Run the offline acceptance harness: run the included sim-workload-suite for 90 minutes at nominal QPS and 30 minutes at 2x expected QPS.
  c. Execute KV cache persistence tests: write/read sequences for 1M keys simulated across shard boundaries.
  d. Run thermals/thermal-cycling in lab for new hardware SKUs: 3 cycles at 80% sustained GPU utilization.
- Exit criteria: all tests green; any critical failure escalated to Release Engineering.

2) Field install & bootstrap checklist
- Owner: Field Engineer (primary), Customer Onsite Technician (secondary).
- Minimum checklist (operator marks pass/fail):
  - [ ] Rack/power verification and PDU mapping matches network diagram.
  - [ ] Firmware baseline (BMC, NIC, GPU firmware) recorded in deployment manifest.
  - [ ] Network ACLs and BGP/peering verified for control-plane proxies.
  - [ ] Local time/sync (NTP/PTP) configured and validated.
  - [ ] HSM/KMS connectivity verified with sample signing operation.
  - [ ] Image accounts and service tokens installed to ephemeral operator account.

3) Hardware & firmware attestation
- Procedure:
  1. Run attestation tooling (hw-attestctl attest --output json) and capture signed statement.
  2. Validate measured boot log and firmware signatures match manifest.
  3. Record telemetry: serial numbers, SKU, NIC MACs, PCB revision, firmware versions.
- Failure modes and mitigations:
  - If measured boot fails: collect logs and isolate node; do not join node to cluster.
  - If firmware mismatch: consult firmware-rollback policy and vendor-supplied signed images.

4) Runtime smoke and KV/prefix cache warmup
- Goals: confirm runtime can load models, serve requests, and persist KV metadata without errors.
- Commands (example snippets):
  - curl -X POST https://local-runtime/healthz -H 'Authorization: Bearer <op-token>'
  - rdbtool kv-sanity --endpoint https://local-kv --verify 10000
- Smoke test checklist:
  - [ ] Model load success for primary model variant (<= 30s cold load).
  - [ ] Inference query at 1 qps/replica returns 95% < 350ms.
  - [ ] KV read/write P99 < 25ms for local SSD-backed KV.

5) Tenant-specific synthetic burn-in (critical section)
- Purpose: expose model-serving, routing, caching, and multitenancy isolation issues prior to production traffic.
- Duration guidance:
  - Small tenants (<= 10 RPS): 6–12 hours.
  - Medium tenants (10–200 RPS): 24–72 hours.
  - Large tenants (> 200 RPS): 72–168 hours with scheduled load ramps.
- Synthetic workload design:
  - Use the tenant's representative prompt set (provided during onboarding) plus fuzzed sequences to exercise length distributions.
  - Include a 10% injection of adversarial/edge prompts to check guardrails.
  - Ramp profile: 0→25% QPS 30 minutes, hold 1h; 25→75% 2h; 75→100% 1h; maintain 100% for X hours as per tenant size.
- Observability checks (automated):
  - Model error rate (bad-inference or empty responses) < 0.5%
  - Token-level cost variance within expected bounds ±15%
  - KV cache hit-rate target: >= 65% after warmup for prefix-heavy workloads
  - Tail latency SLOs: P95 < 300ms, P99 < 700ms (adjust per SLO matrix)
- Operator actions on alarm:
  1. If error rate spikes > 1% for 10 minutes: pause synthetic load, collect core dumps, escalate to runtime-engineering.
  2. If P99 increases by >2x baseline: enable fallback model variant routing and notify customer success.

6) Telemetry validation and evidence collection
- Required telemetry streams:
  - Inference traces (sampling 1/1000 requests or 1% whichever is higher).
  - Token accounting (per-request token counts, model id, quantization flag).
  - Hardware telemetry (GPU temp, power, ECC/memory errors).
  - Network metrics (egress RTT, packet drops), and control-plane heartbeats.
- Evidence bundle to produce for CAT:
  - Signed attestation statement (hardware + firmware).
  - Burn-in report (load profile, duration, pass/fail with timestamps).
  - Observability extract: p95/p99 latencies, error rates, KV hit rates, per-tenant token accounting for the burn-in window.
  - Container/image digests and deployment manifest.
- Storage format: compressed tar.gz with SHA256 checksum and two copies: one uploaded to customer evidence bucket and one retained in Redwood secure evidence store for 90 days.

7) Licensing and KMS rotation (during pre-handoff but part of certification)
- Steps to rotate operator license and customer KMS keys post-install: 
  1. Generate ephemeral rotation token (use operator-rot-tool rotate --mode ephemeral).
  2. Push new key material to HSM via vendor API; confirm key id and wrap key metadata.
  3. Run integration smoke to decrypt a sample secret and sign a token.
  4. Record rotation event to audit log and tag evidence bundle.
- Rollback: if new key fails validation, revert to previous key and schedule controlled re-rotate with vendor support.

8) Customer Acceptance Testing (CAT) and handoff
- CAT acceptance criteria (all must be satisfied):
  - Hardware attestation present and signed.
  - Burn-in completed with no critical failures and all telemetry targets met.
  - Security checklist: KMS attested, agent/collector configured, RBAC bindings verified.
  - Performance checklist: P95 and P99 within SLO band per customer SLA.
- Handoff artifacts provided to customer: operator runbook, evidence bundle, support contact matrix, and rollback playbook.
- Sign-off template: Customer Success provides signed acceptance email referencing the evidence bundle digest and the date/time.

Operator runbook (post-CAT steady-state checks)
- Daily checks (5–10 minutes) by operator or automated job:
  - Verify control-plane heartbeats for all tenants.
  - Ensure telemetry ingest rate is within expected window (alert if < 60% of expected).
  - Check for any ECC or GPU hardware errors reported in last 24h.
- Weekly checks:
  - Refresh of agent TLS certs in staging and canary.
  - Review top-20 slow queries and token cost drift.
- Incident quick actions (first 30 minutes):
  1. If runtime is unresponsive: run safe-degrader (runtimectl degrade --mode read-only) to preserve state while maintaining basic API surface.
  2. If KV corruption suspected: snapshot current state, enable read-only mode, initiate kv-verify job.
  3. If thermal event: move traffic away from affected node(s) and coordinate with field replacement.

Upgrade and rollback guidance (concise)
- Recommended pattern: automated canary → staged rollout → safety window → full rollout.
- Safety gates prior to stage promotion:
  - Canary stable for 2h at canary traffic or 1k requests (whichever greater) with no more than 0.2% error increase.
  - Telemetry ingestion continuity and auto-scaling behaved within thresholds.
- Immediate rollback triggers:
  - Canary error increase > 1% sustained for 10 minutes.
  - P99 latency regression > 2x baseline for 15 minutes.
- Rollback procedure summary:
  1. Pause further promotions.
  2. Promote previous revision for affected replicas using operator canary control panel.
  3. Run smoke tests and confirm with APM traces that service recovered.
  4. Open RCA ticket and engage release engineering.

Checklist: Field certification acceptance matrix (table)
- Represented here as a plain ASCII table for portability. Operators must produce a matrix with checkmarks as part of evidence.

Item | Responsible | Target | Pass criteria
-----|-------------|--------|------------
Hardware attestation | Field Eng | Before join | Signed statement present
Image digests verified | Field Eng | Pre-boot | sha256 match for all images
Model load smoke | Runtime Eng | Post-bootstrap | Primary model loads in <=30s
Synthetic burn-in | Field Eng | Per SLA | Pass per tenant size guidance
Telemetry contract | Observability | During burn-in | Required streams present and sampled
KMS validation | Security | Pre-handoff | Decrypt/sign test succeed
CAT sign-off | Customer Success | Post-burn-in | Signed acceptance and evidence uploaded

Evidence retention and compliance
- Retain evidence bundles for 90 days in secure store; snapshot metadata retained for 3 years per contract.
- For regulated customers, escalate to compliance team for longer retention windows and provide audit-ready exports.

Templates and automation (links and CLI examples)
- burnin-runner.yaml (sample job config)
  - description: config for tenant synthetic run including ramp profile, prompt sets, and fuzz rules.
  - required fields: tenant_id, prompt_set_id, qps_profile, duration_hours, edge_injection_pct
- Example command to run a burn-in job: 
  rdb-burnin submit --tenant tenant-123 --config burnin-runner.yaml --report-out /tmp/burnin-report.tar.gz

Troubleshooting guide (common issues)
- Model fails to load intermittently: check model shard mapping and GPU memory pressure; run gpu-mem-profile and compare to model footprint matrix.
- KV read errors under load: inspect disk IO wait and concurrent garbage collection; consider increasing local IO throughput or moving shards.
- Telemetry gaps: ensure agent has outbound connectivity to ingest endpoints and verify agent policy for sample rate.

Postmortem and RCA expectations for certification failures
- Any certification failure that blocks CAT must produce a 48h preliminary incident report with: timeline, impact, immediate mitigations, owner, and next steps. Full RCA within 7 business days.

Appendices
A. Example burn-in ramp profile YAML (simplified)
---
qps_profile:
  - duration_mins: 30
    target_qps_pct: 25
  - duration_mins: 60
    target_qps_pct: 75
  - duration_mins: 120
    target_qps_pct: 100
edge_injection_pct: 10
prompt_set_id: promptset-tenant-123
---

B. Acceptance email template
Subject: CAT Acceptance - <customer> - <deployment-id>
Body:
We have completed field certification and tenant burn-in for deployment <deployment-id>. Evidence bundle digest: <sha256>. All acceptance criteria met as of <datetime>. Please reply to confirm acceptance.

C. Contact matrix
- Field Eng (on-call): +1-555-0101, field-eng@redwood.ai
- Runtime SRE: runtime-sre@redwood.ai
- Customer Success: cs-team@redwood.ai

D. Quick links
